title: poc-model-choice-quant-prompt-strategy
content:
Purpose:
Quick reference & playbook for model selection, quantization strategy, and prompt/pipeline tuning during customer POCs. This is intentionally pragmatic: help an SE run experiments fast, pick tradeoffs, and produce a short config recommendation for the customer proposal.

Context / customer snapshot:
- Mid-market ecommerce customer (search + summarization + FAQ bot).
- Hard constraints: SLA 200 ms 95p for chat on 1-2k concurrent shoppers; budget target < $X per 1M tokens.
- Data: product descriptions (~1–5 sentences), user reviews, small customer knowledge base (500 docs).
- Preference: avoid onerous model licensing; open models preferred, but can propose managed hosted options if latency/cost justify.

Decision framework (one-liner):
- If >95% of workload is short-context Q/A or embeddings, prioritize smaller, quantized models + heavy caching.
- If user-facing generation with creative length >256 tokens, choose better FP16/8 models and fall back to cached answers for common queries.

Model selection checklist (fast pass):
- Accuracy vs latency: run 3 small evals (search rerank, short answer, long summary) on representative prompt set.
- Candidate model families: LLaMA-2 derivatives, Mistral, Phi-2 (where licensing allows), and community distilled variants.
- Model-size tiers to test: 7B (low-latency baseline), 13B (sweet spot for many POCs), 34B (quality headroom if cost allows).
- For each candidate record: generation quality, avg latency @ batch=1, GPU memory footprint, quantization friendliness (existing 4/8-bit recipes).

Quantization strategy notes (practical):
- Start with static 8-bit (GPTQ / awq) on 13B: fastest path to lower cost with modest quality drop.
- Use 4-bit (gptq/awq+nf4) only after baseline 8-bit eval shows acceptable degradation. Keep a small unquantized FP16/32 variant for QA/regression.
- Quantize per-layer where supported: attention and MLP sensitivity differs — monitor perplexity and key-shot examples.
- When using KV-caching heavy workloads (chat with long histories), prioritize qkv-compat quantization paths that preserve cache layout to avoid regen cost.
- Tooling: prefer the vendor-verified quant artifacts (if available) or use our internal quant harness (linked). Always store checksum + quant metadata in artifact catalog.

Prompt and pipeline tuning (playbook):
- Pipeline stages: user intent classifier -> prompt template injection (context) -> model generation -> post-filter/answer-normalizer -> reranker (if needed).
- Intent classifier: cheap transformer (<1B) at edge to pick short-answer vs generation path. Avoid spinning up big model for 40% of queries that are trivial.
- Prompt templates (examples):
  - Short answer template (for factual Q/A):
    System: "You are a concise product expert. Answer briefly with product attributes and where to buy."
    User: "{user_question}
Context: {doc_snippets}
Answer:"
  - Summarization template:
    System: "Summarize the following reviews into 3 bullets focused on sentiment and defects."
    User: "{reviews_chunk}
Summary:"
- Chain-of-thought: avoid for production unless explicit quality/regulatory need; too costly.
- Temperature: default 0.0–0.2 for factual; 0.6+ for creative recommendations.
- Max tokens: cap based on expected output; set stop sequences to reduce token waste.
- Reranking: use embeddings+dot-product on top-K candidates from a cheap model to avoid running large completion multiple times.

Eval harness (what to run during the POC):
- Datasets: 200 sample queries split by intent, 50 long generation cases, 100 A/B rerank pairs.
- Metrics: exact match / F1 (QA), ROUGE/BLEU for summaries (informative only), human preference sample (n=30), mean latency @ 95p, cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.
- Regression checks: pick 10 golden prompts (customer-specific) and baseline outputs from FP16 model to detect quality cliffs after quant.
- Automation: run nightly microbenchmark (latency & mem) on the chosen infra slice. Store results in shared spreadsheet (link above).

Deployment considerations (hosted vs dedicated vs private):
- Hosted API: fastest to demo but watch multi-tenant noisy neighbors; use dedicated plans if 95p latency SLO required.
- Dedicated: recommend for sustained throughput >X qps or strict data isolation. Easier to pin quant artifacts and kernel selection.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): necessary for regulated docs; plan for heavier ops + model artifact transfer. Quantize locally only after checksum validation.

Cost / performance tradeoffs (rules of thumb):
- 7B quantized (8-bit): lowest cost, best latency; expect lower contextual reasoning. Good for classification/short QA.
- 13B quantized: best sweet spot for many ecommerce POCs — balance of quality & cost.
- 34B FP16: expensive, use for high-value long-form summarization only or as a fallback.

Quick experiment matrix (to run in first 5 business days):
1) Baseline quality: 13B FP16 @ batch=1 — record latency and quality.
2) Quantize 13B -> 8-bit; rerun same eval set, measure delta.
3) Test 7B 8-bit for latency/cost baseline.
4) If 13B quant shows >8% degradation on golden prompts, try 13B 4-bit on subset.
5) Run caching + prefix reuse test on top-10 frequent queries.

Workshop takeaways (notes from customer session):
- Customer cares most about answer correctness for product specs and fast replies on checkout pages.
- They are OK with short-form answers for search snippets but want full product summaries in returns/CSR flows.
- Team expressed concerns about quantization causing hallucinations — recommend visible QA/rollback plan.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Get customer token budget target (finance) — current number is placeholder.
- Confirm whether external review content can be used to fine-tune or only used as context snippets.
- Evaluate latency on customer's preferred cloud region (eu-west) — infra might change GPU choice.
- Action: Aisha to run 13B FP16 -> 8-bit overnight and post results to PR.

Deliverables for proposal:
- Short appendix with 2 recommended configurations:
  A) Cost-conscious: 13B 8-bit quant (hosted) + intent classifier + caching.
  B) Performance-first: 13B FP16 on Dedicated GPUs + 34B FP16 fallback for heavy summaries.
- Artifacts: evaluation spreadsheet, quant checksums, prompt templates, replay scripts.

Notes to self:
- Keep templates lean; customers copy them directly into code.
- Flag model license compatibility in the final doc.
- If time, produce side-by-side audio/video demo to show latency differences.

References / useful links:
- internal quant guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Infra/Quantization+recipes
- prompt templates repo: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-templates
- SE POC checklist (canonical): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/POC+checklist
